Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 1) Professional infamous conduct means:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.option1: Failure of patient to follow advice
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.option2: Refusal of patient to pay fees
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: Professional infamous conduct is any dishonourable or unethical act by a doctor that goes against medical ethics and professional standards.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 2) Improper conduct with a patient or patient’s relative is called:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: In professional infamous conduct, adultery means improper sexual or personal conduct with a patient or patient’s relative.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 3) Performing criminal abortion by a doctor is:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: Criminal or illegal abortion is included under professional infamous conduct. It is also a serious medico-legal offence.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 4) Advertising or canvassing for patients is known as:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: Advertisement means promoting oneself or canvassing for patients. It is listed as professional infamous conduct.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 5) Association with unqualified practitioners is:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: A registered doctor should not associate professionally with unqualified practitioners. It lowers professional standards and is infamous conduct.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 6) Drug addiction affecting medical practice is:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: Addiction becomes professional infamous conduct when it affects a doctor’s ability to practise safely and ethically.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 7) Practising medicine under alcohol influence is:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: Alcoholism affecting professional practice is included in professional infamous conduct because it endangers patient care.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 8) Conviction for an offence involving moral turpitude is:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: Conviction for offences involving moral turpitude, except political offences, may amount to professional infamous conduct.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 9) Violation of drug laws by a doctor is called:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: Contravention or violation of the Drug Act is included in professional infamous conduct.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 10) Assisting an unqualified person to practise medicine is:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: Covering means helping or allowing an unqualified person to practise medicine under a doctor’s name or protection.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 11) Fee splitting or commission for referral is called:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: Dichotomy means fee splitting or receiving commission for referrals. It is professional infamous conduct.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 12) Revealing confidential patient information without justification is:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: Unjustified disclosure of confidential information violates professional secrecy. It is included under professional infamous conduct.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 13) Unfair criticism of a fellow doctor is called:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: Depreciation of professional brethren means unfairly criticizing another doctor. It is considered unethical professional conduct.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 14) Issuing false medical certificates is:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: False certificates, false reports or false documents are serious professional misconduct and may lead to disciplinary action.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 15) Denying treatment only because of patient’s religion is:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: Refusal of service on religious grounds is unethical. It violates the principle of non-discrimination in medical care.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 16) Medical negligence is also called:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: Medical negligence or malpraxis means failure to exercise reasonable care and skill, causing harm to the patient.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 17) The essential element of medical negligence is:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.option4: Harm due to lack of reasonable care
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: Negligence requires failure of reasonable care and skill resulting in patient harm. Mere dissatisfaction is not enough.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 18) Refusal to admit an urgent case is:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: Refusing to admit an urgent case is listed under civil negligence. It is failure to provide expected care.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 19) Failure to obtain informed consent is:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: Failure to obtain informed consent is a civil negligence issue. Consent is required before procedures and treatment decisions.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 20) Failure to examine a patient properly is:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: Not examining the patient is a failure of reasonable care. It is included under civil negligence.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 21) Delayed attendance by a doctor causing harm is:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: Failure to attend or delayed attendance can amount to civil negligence if it causes harm to the patient.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 22) Wrong diagnosis due to lack of care or skill is:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: Wrong diagnosis due to lack of reasonable care is civil negligence. It differs from an unavoidable diagnostic difficulty.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 23) Negligent performance of a procedure is:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: If a procedure is performed carelessly and harm occurs, it is civil negligence.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 24) Failure to immunize when indicated is:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: Failure to immunize when it is medically indicated is a failure of expected care and falls under civil negligence.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 25) Failure to perform indicated investigations is:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: Not advising or performing necessary investigations may cause diagnostic delay and is considered civil negligence.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 26) Failure to interpret an X-ray correctly is:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: X-ray interpretation error due to lack of care or skill is listed under civil negligence.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 27) Failure to arrange a substitute doctor is:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: A doctor should arrange substitute care when needed. Failure to do so may harm the patient and is civil negligence.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 28) Failure to provide postoperative care is:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: Postoperative care is a duty of the doctor. Failure to provide it is a form of civil negligence.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 29) Premature discharge of a patient is:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: Discharging a patient before it is safe can cause harm. It is listed as civil negligence.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 30) Grossly incompetent administration of anaesthesia is:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: Severe anaesthesia error causing serious harm is classified as criminal negligence because it reflects gross incompetence.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 31) Performing illegal abortion by a doctor is:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: Criminal abortion is specifically included under criminal negligence. It may also be professional infamous conduct.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 32) Gross negligence during labour or delivery is:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: Delivery mismanagement with gross negligence is a criminal negligence example due to serious risk to mother or baby.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 33) Leaving a sponge inside the abdomen is:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: Retained foreign body such as sponge or instrument inside the body is criminal negligence.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 34) Leaving a surgical instrument inside body is:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: A retained surgical instrument is a serious preventable error and falls under criminal negligence.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 35) Administration of a wrong drug causing serious harm is:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: Wrong drug or substance causing serious harm, such as blindness, is an example of criminal negligence.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 36) Operation on the wrong limb is:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: Wrong patient, wrong limb or wrong finger operation is classified as criminal negligence.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 37) Wrong-patient surgery is:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: Operating on the wrong patient is a grave preventable error. It is treated as criminal negligence.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 38) Negligence by a hospital or healthcare institution is:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: Corporate negligence means negligence by the hospital or healthcare institution, not only by an individual doctor.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 39) Patient’s own negligence contributing to injury is:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: Contributory negligence occurs when the patient’s own careless behaviour contributes to the injury.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 40) A patient ignores medical advice and worsens his condition. This is:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: When patient’s own action or inaction contributes to harm, it is contributory negligence.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 41) Penal erasure from BM&DC register may occur due to:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: Penal erasure is one cause of removal of a doctor’s name from the BM&DC register and occurs due to professional infamous conduct.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 42) Entry made in error or fraud in BM&DC register may lead to:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: If a registration entry is made by error or fraud, the doctor’s name may be erased from the BM&DC register.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 43) Erasure from BM&DC register after death is:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: Death is listed as one of the causes of erasure of name from the BM&DC register.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 44) Penal erasure is called:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: Penal erasure is called professional death sentence because the doctor loses legal rights and privileges of a registered practitioner.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 45) Loss of legal rights as a registered doctor occurs in:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: Penal erasure removes the doctor from the BM&DC register. Therefore, the doctor loses privileges of registered medical practice.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 46) A doctor receives commission for sending patients to a diagnostic centre. This is:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: Commission or fee splitting for referrals is dichotomy. It is professional infamous conduct.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 47) A doctor allows an unqualified person to treat patients under his name. This is:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: Covering means assisting an unqualified person to practise medicine. It is a classic professional infamous conduct.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 48) A doctor issues a fake fitness certificate. This is:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: Issuing false medical certificates, reports or documents is professional infamous conduct.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 49) A doctor publicly and unfairly criticizes another doctor to attract patients. This is:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: Unfair criticism of fellow doctors is depreciation of professional brethren and is considered unethical.

Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.question: 50) A hospital fails to maintain safe systems and a patient is harmed. This is:
Professional Infamous Conduct & Malpraxi.exp: When institutional failure causes harm, it is corporate negligence. Responsibility lies with the healthcare institution or hospital system.
